[spoiler= quick blow by blow of what Koranvistan's past looks like- a more detailed but WIP write-up in my overview]
History that doesn't matter:
-Pre 1100's: Koranvistan and Kyraniya did not exist, as Kyraniyans hadn't even settled in the area yet
-1100's to the 1300's: Kyraniyans settled in the region, loosely organized by clan and affiliated territories.
-1400's to 1589: Kyraniya was one of several small kingdoms in the area, but grew in power during this time.

History that matters more:
-1589 to 1893: Kyraniya/Koranvistan was a more well-established kingdom during this time. It accumulated wealth and military prestige due to a somewhat central location. Kyrkagrad and Andrudin were large, merchant cities with diverse, bustling cultures. Notable parts about this era are the Kingdom's emphasis on education, social progress, and free trade. The University at Velnaz was well funded in this time, and boasted a thorough education for every one that walked through the doors.
-1893 to 2026: Koranvistan, pushed by the Orthodox church, transitioned to a Republic. The republican government was extremely right-wing, undoing almost all progressive reforms (Freedom of religion, marriage equality, good wages for the working class). There were three presidents under the republic. The last, Phillipp Petrenkov, nearly ruined the nation by funneling wealth into the pockets of foreign and domestic oil and gas barons.
-2026 to 2027: The Revolution was led by Elena Marniy-Kovach Markov and members of her family, friends, and other rebels for which life in the Republic was untenable. Beaten down by wealth and income inequality, lack of personal freedoms, and the increased violation of Koranvistani's rights to life, rebels stormed and seized areas around the city of Andrudin. From this foothold, with a several-nation liberation front, the rebels seized control of the nation and reinstated the monarchy with system of representatives. Progressive reforms were pushed as the nation began an economic upturn.[/spoiler]

It can be both; it largely depends on context.

For example, the Nationality "German" would be all people who are citizens of the Federal Republic of Germany
(The definition of nationality is "the status of belonging to a particular nation.")

While the ethnicity "German" refers to all Germans living in countries such as Austria, Germany, and Switzerland, as well as separate Germanic linguistic groups like Saxons and Bavarians. And German diaspora groups like German Americans.

The literal definition of ethnicity is "a shared cultural heritage, including language, religion, and traditions, that connects a group of people through a common ancestry and histor.y"
